---
title: "IBGE Census - Census tract harmonisation"
format: html
editor: visual
---

This code links 2010 and 2022 census tracts based on their largest spatial overlap in both directions, creating a correspondence table (crosswalk). It identifies whether areas stayed the same, were split, merged, or changed in a more complex way. The final layer keeps the 2022 census tract boundaries unchanged and records their relationship with the 2010 areas.

```{r libraries}
#| message: false

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(igraph)
```

```{r data_import}

census_tract_2010 <- st_read("IBGE/Data/ibge_census_tracts.gpkg", layer = "2010")
census_tract_2022 <- st_read("IBGE/Data/ibge_census_tracts.gpkg", layer = "2022")
```

![Census tract harmonization flow chart](images/Harmonizing%202010%20and%202022%20Census%20Tracts.png){fig-align="center" width="461"}

```{r harmonisation}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare 2010 and 2022 census tracts
# ------------------------------------------------------------

t2010 <- census_tract_2010 %>%
  st_transform(5880) %>%
  st_set_precision(1e6) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  select(id_2010 = code_tract)

t2022 <- census_tract_2022 %>%
  st_transform(5880) %>%
  st_set_precision(1e6) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  select(id_2022 = code_tract)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build bidirectional largest-overlap crosswalk
#
# 2022 -> 2010:
# each 2022 tract gets its main 2010 match
#
# 2010 -> 2022:
# each 2010 tract gets its main 2022 match
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fwd <- st_join(
  t2022,
  t2010,
  largest = TRUE
) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(id_2010, id_2022) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(id_2010),
    !is.na(id_2022)
  )


bwd <- st_join(
  t2010,
  t2022,
  largest = TRUE
) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(id_2010, id_2022) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(id_2010),
    !is.na(id_2022)
  )


crosswalk <- bind_rows(
  fwd,
  bwd
) %>%
  distinct()


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build connected 2010-2022 relationship groups
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g <- graph_from_data_frame(
  crosswalk %>%
    transmute(
      from = paste0("y2010_", id_2010),
      to   = paste0("y2022_", id_2022)
    ),
  directed = FALSE
)


comp <- components(g)


id_lookup <- tibble(
  node = names(comp$membership),
  common_id = as.integer(comp$membership)
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Add common_id to crosswalk
# ------------------------------------------------------------

crosswalk_grouped <- crosswalk %>%
  mutate(
    common_id = id_lookup$common_id[
      match(
        paste0("y2010_", id_2010),
        id_lookup$node
      )
    ]
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Classify the relationship in each connected group
# ------------------------------------------------------------

group_sizes <- crosswalk_grouped %>%
  group_by(common_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_2010 = n_distinct(id_2010),
    n_2022 = n_distinct(id_2022),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    relationship = case_when(
      n_2010 == 1 & n_2022 == 1 ~ "1:1",
      
      n_2010 == 1 & n_2022 > 1 ~
        "2010_to_2022_split",
      
      n_2010 > 1 & n_2022 == 1 ~
        "2010_to_2022_merge",
      
      n_2010 > 1 & n_2022 > 1 ~
        "many_to_many"
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Create lookup for each 2022 tract
#
# IMPORTANT:
# no 2022 geometries are changed here
# ------------------------------------------------------------

lookup_2022 <- crosswalk_grouped %>%
  distinct(
    id_2022,
    common_id
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    group_sizes,
    by = "common_id"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Create lookup for 2010 tracts
#
# A 2010 tract can appear multiple times if it relates to
# multiple 2022 tracts
# ------------------------------------------------------------

lookup_2010 <- crosswalk_grouped %>%
  left_join(
    group_sizes,
    by = "common_id"
  ) %>%
  select(
    id_2010,
    id_2022,
    common_id,
    n_2010,
    n_2022,
    relationship
  ) %>%
  distinct()


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Final base layer
#
# 2022 geometry is preserved exactly.
# Nothing is dissolved or split.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

base_geom_2022 <- t2022 %>%
  left_join(
    lookup_2022,
    by = "id_2022"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    base_id = paste0("t2022_", id_2022)
  ) %>%
  select(
    base_id,
    id_2022,
    common_id,
    n_2010,
    n_2022,
    relationship,
    everything()
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Sanity checks
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Should equal the number of original 2022 tracts
nrow(t2022)
nrow(base_geom_2022)


# Every 2022 tract should remain unique
base_geom_2022 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    unique_2022 = n_distinct(id_2022)
  )


# Relationship distribution
group_sizes %>%
  count(
    relationship,
    sort = TRUE
  )


# Number of 2022 tracts in each relationship type
base_geom_2022 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  count(
    relationship,
    sort = TRUE
  )


# Inspect many-to-many cases
lookup_2022 %>%
  filter(
    relationship == "many_to_many"
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    desc(n_2010 + n_2022)
  ) %>%
  head(20)
```

Be aware that the base geometry layer has not been unioned by common ID. 2010 tracts that were split share a common ID but still follow the 2022 tract boundaries.
